issue_context.title: [Feature] Allow request interception chaining (was 'based on request method')
comments: I find the snippet in the proposal to be less readable than the original one - two callbacks per call are harder to work with. Options.method can be added, but I'd like to better understand the exact use cases it addresses.
So why can't you use `endpoints[endpointName].method` in your `intercept` fixture?

The issue is that we can't intercept both GET and POST requests individually at the same time because:
* the matcher `<string|RegExp|function(URL):boolean>` provides only the `url` so we can't match by method.
* the handler `<function(Route, Request)>` can match by method but once you are in a handler, you can't "skip" it, if it's not the right method, and go to the next matcher/handler. If we intercept both `getItem` and `createItem`, we'll always hit the last registered interceptor with path `/api/items` (`createItem` in this example) and there will be no way to fall back to `getItem` because `// There is no chaining, first handler wins.` 

We can have `getItemsAndCreateItem` interceptor that combines both but this doesn't feel right :)

We've started hitting these limitations too, specifically "There is no chaining, first handler wins.".

Engineers, after using tools like Cypress, expect that if they use `route.continue()`, the request will "bubble up" to the next handler. They also expect to be able to handle POST and GET separately.

We'll add more custom tooling to our project to help mitigate the issue, but an implementation on the Playwright side would be amazing.

I quite like the interface that MSW offers (as an example): https://mswjs.io/

~@[mrmckeb](https://github.com/mrmckeb) would you mind filing a request for bubbling? That one I think we should implement, we were waiting for the user request.~

Ah, after reading last @[purepear](https://github.com/purepear) update it seems like original request is also about chaining! Let's fix it under this issue then.
